mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW X6 40i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW X6 40i engine replacement typically costs £2,500-£5,000 supply-only for a reconditioned B58, or £3,500-£5,800 for a rebuilt unit. Fitted by a specialist, expect £4,500-£8,000 total. B58B30C (2019-2020) reconditioned: £2,500-£4,200 supply-only. B58B30M1 (2020-2023) reconditioned: £2,800-£4,500 supply-only. B58B30P (2023+) reconditioned: £3,200-£5,000 supply-only. Professional fitting adds £1,500-£2,500 depending on your location and workshop.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of B58 engine problems in a BMW X6 40i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common warning signs of B58 issues include low coolant warnings, reduced power (drivetrain malfunction), and unusual noises from the engine bay. Low coolant light may indicate expansion tank cracks or system leaks. Drivetrain malfunction with loss of boost often points to charge pipe failure. Whining noises may indicate water pump or PCV system issues. Check engine lights require immediate diagnosis - the B58 is robust but not invincible.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a high-mileage BMW X6 40i?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a G06 X6 40i worth £35,000-£60,000, engine replacement (£3,500-£5,800 supply-only) typically represents 10-20% of the vehicle's value - making it a financially viable option for most owners. Compare replacement cost against vehicle value - replacement is viable up to roughly 60-70% of the car's value. Given the high vehicle value, replacement is usually justified if the body and interior are in excellent condition. Low-mileage, well-serviced, or cherished 40i examples justify the investment. Always factor the 12-month warranty into your decision.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW X6 40i B58 engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B58 is widely considered BMW's most reliable modern petrol engine. With proper maintenance, 150,000-200,000 miles is achievable before major work. Regular oil changes (every 8,000-10,000 miles) are critical for longevity. Coolant system components (expansion tank, water pump) are wear items - replace every 60,000-80,000 miles as preventative maintenance. The B58's closed-deck design and robust internals make it exceptionally durable. Charge pipe failure is the most common boost-related issue - upgraded aluminium pipes are a permanent fix.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the B58B30C, B58B30M1 and B58B30P engines in the X6 40i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B58B30C (2019-2020) is the initial G06 X6 40i engine producing 340hp. The B58B30M1 (2020-2023) is a production refinement with the same power output. The B58B30P (2023+) introduced 48V mild-hybrid assistance, increasing power to 381hp and adding 12hp electric boost. B58B30C and B58B30M1: 340hp, no mild-hybrid. B58B30P: 381hp with 48V MHEV, improved fuel economy and smoother stop-start. All are 3.0L (2998cc) straight-six turbo petrol engines. Engine bays are similar - replacement is direct bolt-in for the correct generation.

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my BMW X6 40i engine with a diesel engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Swapping a 40i's B58 petrol for a diesel (xDrive30d/40d B57) is technically complex and rarely cost-effective. The engines have different mounts, wiring looms, ECUs, cooling systems, and fuel systems. B58 is a 3.0L petrol; B57 is a 3.0L diesel - fuel system, ECU and exhaust are completely different. Transmission may also differ - petrol and diesel X6s use different gearbox calibrations. Insurance must be notified of any non-standard engine swap. Stick to like-for-like code-matching for warranty coverage and straightforward installation.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW X6 40i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW X6 40i was introduced with the third-generation G06 X6 in 2019, replacing the xDrive35i as the core petrol model. Powered by the B58B30 - BMW's award-winning 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six - the 40i delivers 340-381hp depending on market and model year, with later LCI models gaining 48V mild-hybrid assistance.

Continued production of xDrive40i with B58B30P, now standard MHEV across all variants

commonProblems.h2: BMW X6 40i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW X6 40i's B58 3.0-litre turbo straight-six is widely considered one of BMW's most refined and durable engines. However, like all modern turbocharged petrol engines, it has known weak points - primarily in the cooling system and charge air plumbing. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded cooling components and charge pipes addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Coolant Loss - Why the BMW X6 40i B58 Loses Coolant
problems.rootCause: The B58's plastic coolant expansion tank and integrated supply lines develop hairline cracks under thermal cycling. Coolant slowly leaks, triggering low coolant warnings. If ignored, the engine can overheat, potentially warping the aluminium cylinder head - though the B58 has robust protection systems that typically prevent catastrophic damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace coolant expansion tank and supply line, bleed cooling system
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if low coolant warning appears but no overheating

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace expansion tank, water pump, thermostat, coolant pipes
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended on high-mileage B58 (80,000+ miles) as preventative maintenance

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt B58 with upgraded cooling components; 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only required in extreme overheating cases - rare on B58

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical G06 X6 40i (2019-2025) is worth approximately £35,000-£60,000 depending on condition and mileage. Expansion tank replacement at a specialist (£300-£500) is cheap insurance. Full engine replacement (£5,500-£8,000 supply-only) typically represents 10-20% of the vehicle's value - making it a financially viable option if required.
problems.recommendation: The B58 is BMW's most reliable modern petrol engine, and full replacement is rarely needed. However, the expansion tank failure is real - and ignoring low coolant warnings eventually leads to overheating. For under £500 at a specialist, replacement is cheap insurance. Keep a bottle of BMW-approved coolant in the boot of your G06 X6 40i and check levels monthly.

problems.h4: Charge Pipe Failure - Why the BMW X6 40i B58 Loses Boost
problems.rootCause: The B58's plastic charge pipe between the intercooler and throttle body is known to be fragile and can crack under boost pressure. The pipe is exposed to heat cycling and engine movement, causing stress fractures. When it fails, the engine loses boost pressure, triggering a drivetrain malfunction warning and reduced power.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable but OEM plastic may fail again - upgraded aluminium recommended

repairOptions.longevity: Recommended on any B58, especially if tuned or driven hard

repairOptions.longevity: Only required if boost leak caused lean-running damage - rare

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical G06 X6 40i is worth £35,000-£60,000. Charge pipe replacement at a specialist (£350-£700) is a modest repair. Upgrading to an aluminium pipe is a one-time fix that costs marginally more than OEM plastic.
problems.recommendation: On any X6 40i, replacing the charge pipe with an upgraded aluminium unit is sensible preventative maintenance. The OEM plastic pipe is a known weak point - and failure leaves you stranded with a car in limp mode. At £400-£700, an upgraded pipe is cheap insurance for a car worth £35,000+.

problems.recommendation: If you experience stop-start issues or battery warnings, have the 48V system diagnosed promptly. Specialist replacement is typically 30-40% cheaper than dealer pricing. For cars approaching 80,000 miles, consider preventative 48V battery inspection as part of routine maintenance.
